pr.title: Fit an install on one screen: build output goes to a log, shown in a dimmed window
pr.head: b80c9555787ffda6f6cf85e01ed05b9807479c86

summary: Field’s installer builds the command-line tool, user interface, audio daemon, and worker environments. Compiler and package-manager output can bury its status rows. This change captures that output in one temporary log and displays a short, temporary window while a command runs.
Successful targets remove the log. A failed command prints its own final 20 lines and keeps the complete log. FIELD_VERBOSE=1 restores streaming output and makes no log.

cards.title: Review result
cards.html: The review found one terminal-display defect: wide characters can wrap despite truncation, leaving output behind after redraw. All 130 focused installer and upgrade tests passed; those tests run without a terminal.

groups.title: Build output stays in a temporary window
groups.kicker: One wrapper captures output and reports failures
intro: Each build or setup command now goes through step, which captures both output streams in a private temporary file. Commands keep their exit status and read no interactive input.

A terminal shows the command and its last five output lines. The window redraws in place and erases itself after the command. Redirected output shows only the installer’s own rows, while a failure prints the end of the failed command and the log path.

files.note: Adds command logging, terminal redraw, failure reporting, and cleanup, then wraps the existing build and setup commands.

checks.text: Wide characters occupy two terminal columns, but the substring limit counts characters. A 20-column terminal received 34 columns of output while redraw still assumed one row, leaving old output behind.
The focused installer tests verified that failure output names the failed native build and retains its log. Successful targets remove logs, and verbose mode streams output without creating one.
Cleanup runs after the target succeeds. An earlier failure exits before cleanup, retaining the log for diagnosis.

files.note: Adds isolated temporary logs and checks quiet output, failure diagnostics, and verbose mode.

checks.text: Ran the installer and upgrade suites: 130 tests passed. The new quiet-output test checks that package-manager output is absent and the temporary directory is empty after success.
These tests capture stdout and stderr through pipes. They cover logs and exit behavior, while terminal cursor movement needs separate terminal coverage.

groups.title: Installer output is part of the install contract
groups.kicker: The reference and plan describe the new output modes
intro: The install reference explains where command output goes, what a failure prints, and how to restore streaming output. The project plan records the same behavior for checkout and release installs.

files.note: Documents the temporary window, retained failure logs, and FIELD_VERBOSE.
Records the quiet-output design in section 2.8.

checks.text: This addition changes the output design of the existing install project. It does not change the plan’s readiness status or introduce an unanswered design question.
